phases.name: Password-less accounts and provisioning claims (foundations, no scenario un-pended)

steps.name: Accounts may exist without a password
criteria: Migration 0016 makes users.password_hash nullable: additive, no backfill, no default; existing hashes and users.email_lower UNIQUE unchanged (DDD-13)
A user row without a password hash is found by email and by id as a password-less account, not a decode error (DDD-13, DDD-21)
The password form refuses a password-less account with the unknown-address status, body and timing, verifying the known-bad hash and recording the attempt (DDD-19, D7)
Forgot-password for a password-less account renders the usual page and sends a link; completing the reset sets a password the password door accepts (DDD-21)
Integration tests prove the above; no acceptance scenario un-pended; all existing suites green; fmt, clippy -D warnings, check-arch pass
steps.scenario_name: an account with no password is found by email, refused at the password door like an unknown address, and can be given a password through reset
steps.description: Compiler-driven change: make the password hash optional end to end so a federated-only account can exist, and route that case through the shipped non-enumerable paths (known-bad-hash verification at the password door, unconditional forgot-password page, reset UPDATE that fills a NULL). Every other reader of the hash (invite accept, bootstrap, admin CLI, services) handles the no-password case explicitly; no sentinel string. No provisioning yet. Proven here at integration level, end to end in 02-02.
steps.implementation_notes: Latest migration is 0015_project_lanes.sql. 0016 is ONE-WAY once a NULL-hash row exists (DDD-13 addendum): no down migration; a revert is a forward migration. Let the compiler enumerate the ~50 readers across 9 crates after changing the store row type to an optional hash; many grep hits are SQL inserts in tests that need no change. DDD-19 forbids short-circuiting on a missing hash: that would be a timing oracle for 'this address has an SSO-only account'. DDD-21: submit_forgot and submit_reset need no logic change beyond the type change. Build the acceptance binary (cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --test acceptance --no-run) before running any lane; the default lane has a known us-04 rolling-upgrade flake, rerun slice3 alone before calling it a regression.

steps.name: foundry-oidc exposes realm roles and profile names
criteria: A validated identity exposes realm_access.roles, name and preferred_username; a token lacking them validates exactly as today, with no roles and no names (DDD-14)
Only realm roles are exposed for the provision decision; resource_access client roles never count; role matching is exact and case-sensitive (OD-9)
A blank, whitespace-only or unset provision role means provisioning off; a non-blank one is carried through the provider read-only (AC-6.1, unit test)
foundry-oidc still depends on neither foundry-store nor foundry-auth; it extracts claims and never decides
Existing foundry-oidc tests and base keycloak-sso behaviour stay green; fmt, clippy -D warnings, check-arch pass

steps.description: Layer-1 claim extraction for D3a: extend the ID-token claim set with Keycloak's realm-role mapper shape and the two profile names the display-name chain needs, all defaulting so older tokens are unaffected, and expose the configured provision role from the provider.
steps.implementation_notes: DISTILL already added OidcConfig.provision_role and with_provision_role (config parsing only) and the env read of FOUNDRY_OIDC_PROVISION_ROLE; confirm blank-means-off is honoured and add the unit test. phases.name: Role-gated provisioning on first Keycloak sign-in (US-06)

steps.name: OIDC callback provisions a member holding the provision role
criteria: A verified newcomer holding the role arrives signed in, greeted by name, with exactly one member membership in the oldest workspace (AC-6.2, DDD-16, DDD-17)
Greeting name is the first non-blank of name, preferred_username, email local-part at most 64 characters; longer candidates are skipped, never truncated (AC-6.3, DDD-18)
Existing accounts link regardless of role; otherwise provisioning off, missing role, or no workspace refuse byte-identically to a wrong password, creating nothing (DDD-15, AC-6.4)
Two concurrent first sign-ins for one address yield one password-less member account and both succeed; admin is never granted (DDD-16, store integration test)
Scenarios 1-7 un-pended and green; refusal reasons and the provision log line covered by unit tests (DDD-20); fmt, clippy -D warnings, check-arch pass
steps.scenario_name: A newcomer holding the provision role is given an account and signed in
steps.description: Walking skeleton for US-06: extend oidc::callback with the DDD-15 find-or-provision order (after the unchanged exchange and email_verified checks: link existing by email_lower with role ignored; provisioning off -> refuse; role absent -> refuse; no workspace -> refuse; else provision), a single-transaction store operation that inserts a password-less user plus one member membership into the original workspace (ON CONFLICT on email_lower then re-read, never touching an existing row), then the shared signin::establish_session seam. Logging per DDD-20: new refusal reasons 'identity lacks provision role' and 'no workspace to provision into' via refuse(); one info line 'oidc identity provisioned' with user id and workspace id, no claims; nothing added to the response. Un-pends scenarios 1-7: 'A newcomer holding the provision role is given an account and signed in' (walking skeleton); 'A newcomer the provider gives no usable full name is still greeted by a name' (3 examples); 'A newcomer without the provision role is turned away' (2 examples); 'With provisioning switched off a newcomer is turned away even holding the role'; 'A newcomer whose address the provider has not confirmed is turned away'; 'Before anyone has claimed the instance a newcomer holding the role is turned away'; 'A member who already has an account keeps it when they hold the provision role'. Scenarios 3-7 are green-by-inheritance guards un-pended together with scenario 1.
steps.implementation_notes: Callback is at crates/foundry-app/src/oidc.rs (callback ~line 163, refuse ~line 59). DDD-17: the existing workspace read is ORDER BY id DESC (newest) - do not reuse it; the original workspace is ORDER BY created_at, id LIMIT 1. An unclaimed instance (no workspace) must refuse so the bootstrap claim ('a workspace exists') cannot be pre-empted (D5). DDD-6 establish_session and DDD-11 refusal function are reused verbatim. The concurrent-first-sign-in race is a store-level test, not an acceptance scenario (DISTILL review). Un-pend by removing @pending from the scenarios in this file only. Lane: cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --test acceptance --no-run first (a cold binary makes subprocess scenarios time out), then FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=keycloak-sso-provisioning cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --test acceptance. Default-lane us-04 rolling-upgrade flake is known; rerun slice3 alone before treating it as a regression.

A provisioned member resets via forgot-password, sets a password, signs in at the password door and reaches the board (AC-6.7, DDD-21)

steps.scenario_name: The operator signs in with their cluster identity and reaches their board
steps.description: Close the DISTILL-era RED gap now that AppState.oidc and InProcHarness::spawn_with_oidc exist (c755003, used by feature_keycloak_sso_provisioning.rs:182). Replace the plain-harness-then-record-issuer Given with a real spawn_with_oidc harness, replace the fake callback (state=from-cookie, no /authorize visit, cookie_store jar) with the full browser round-trip, make account Givens create real rows, and finish the Thens that currently panic! as DELIVER placeholders. Then un-pend the walking skeleton and the rest of US-01. Named faults the 5 scenarios must kill: (F1) the sign-in page never renders the cluster-identity control when a provider is configured (offer_oidc forced false) - scenario 2; (F2) start reuses one state/nonce across attempts - scenario 3; (F3) callback omits the Max-Age=0 challenge-cookie clear on success - scenario 5; (F4) callback redirects to / without establishing a session, or establishes it for a different user - scenarios 1 and 4; (F5) a federated session is scoped to a workspace or user other than the account's, so the filed issue is not authored by them - scenario 4.
steps.implementation_notes: PRODUCTION ALREADY SHIPPED (base flow c755003 v0.4.0, D3a 9abf827). A scenario that passes on first run against existing code is EXPECTED: record it honestly as green-on-first-run in the step's RED/GREEN log, never fabricate a RED. A scenario that fails must fail for a business reason (wrong status, absent control, absent session, wrong author) - not for a harness reason (dropped Secure cookie, missing /authorize visit, unseeded account); harness failures are fixed in the step module, not in production. Any production fix is minimal and named after the scenario that exposed it; oidc.rs and signin.rs are listed only in case. D3/D3a: base scenarios run with provisioning OFF - build the OidcConfig as the provisioning module's spawn_foundry does but with with_provision_role(None) (or omit it); that is D3 behaviour exactly. No scenario in this step conflicts with D3a. Shared helpers (set_cookie_pair, cookie_value, mask_csrf, password_attempt, the start->authorize->callback round-trip) already exist in feature_keycloak_sso_provisioning.rs: prefer making them pub(crate) or moving them to a support module over copying them; that file is listed for that reason only and its behaviour must not change (us-06 lane is the guard). cucumber-rs step text is global: keep the 'cluster identity' wording, do not add a phrase that collides with us_06_signin or the provisioning module. Scenario 4: file the issue through the shipped HTTP issue-filing route with the federated session cookie and CSRF token; read the author at the store boundary in the Then. Linking by non-normalised email is NOT killed here (the base account and the vouched address share case); provisioning scenario 7 already covers it - do not claim it. OD-10 (role revocation) is out of scope; do not touch provisioning scenario 11. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: Layer-3 acceptance un-pending over real HTTP and real Postgres is example-based (Mandates 9/11); no new unit-level contract is introduced. ENVIRONMENT: build with CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_BUILD_OVERRIDE_STRIP=false on this host; warm the acceptance binary first (cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --test acceptance --no-run) - a cold binary makes subprocess scenarios time out; acceptance uses a PREBUILT foundry binary for subprocess lanes, so rebuild foundry before any lane that launches it; bound EVERY lane run with a timeout and kill leftover containers if it hangs. steps.scenario_name: An identity with no foundry account is turned away
steps.description: Prove the link-only gate of the shipped callback with provisioning off: a stranger is refused and nothing is created, a matching account at an unconfirmed address is refused, an existing account with no membership fails closed in the shared establish_session seam. Named faults the 3 scenarios must kill: (F6) email_verified check removed from the callback - scenario 'An unconfirmed address...'; (F7) an unset provision role treated as 'provision anyone' (judge_newcomer allows None) - scenario 'An identity with no foundry account...' via the no-account-created Then; (F8) the refusal names its reason (e.g. 'no such account') instead of the generic copy - same scenario via the refused-uniformly Then; (F9) establish_session's no-membership branch defaults to some workspace instead of failing closed - scenario 'A person who belongs to no workspace...'.
steps.implementation_notes: PRODUCTION ALREADY SHIPPED: green-on-first-run is expected and must be recorded honestly; a failure must be a business failure; any production fix minimal. D3a INTERACTION (the step where it matters): these scenarios assume link-only. They MUST run with FOUNDRY_OIDC_PROVISION_ROLE effectively unset (spawn_with_oidc config with no provision role), which is D3 behaviour exactly: the callback's judge_newcomer returns 'no foundry account for this identity' and provisions nothing. Under D3a with a role configured AND held, 'An identity with no foundry account is turned away' would instead provision and sign the person in - not a contradiction at runtime because the scenario's Given ('foundry is connected to the cluster identity provider') is the default, provisioning-off configuration, but the feature header comment ('It provisions nothing (D3)') predates D3a; reported as an open question, Gherkin NOT edited. 'A person who belongs to no workspace' concerns an EXISTING account: under D3a an existing account links regardless of role, then establish_session fails closed - consistent with D3a. The unconfirmed check precedes find-or-provision in both D3 and D3a - consistent. The refused-uniformly Then today only checks status and two forbidden phrases; strengthening it to compare against a real wrong-password answer (mask_csrf) is welcome in the step module but must not change Gherkin. OD-10 out of scope. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: Layer-3 example-based acceptance (Mandates 9/11). ENVIRONMENT: CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_BUILD_OVERRIDE_STRIP=false for cargo builds on this host; warm the acceptance binary first; acceptance uses a prebuilt foundry binary for subprocess lanes; bound every lane run with a timeout. GUARD LANES: keycloak-sso tag lane; keycloak-sso-provisioning (us-06) lane; cargo xtask check-arch; cargo xtask smoke.

Each forged or stale arrival gets the generic 401 refusal and no session; the wrong-challenge arrival carries a genuine challenge cookie with a state that does not match it

The identity-shaped variants (stale nonce, unpublished key, foreign issuer, lapsed) are exercised through a genuine start and /authorize visit, so the refusal comes from validation of the minted identity, not from a missing challenge

steps.scenario_name: An arrival nobody started is refused
steps.description: Prove the callback's challenge checks and foundry-oidc's ID-token validation against the issuer double's mint variants. Named faults the 6 scenarios must kill: (F10) callback proceeds without a challenge cookie - 'An arrival nobody started...'; (F11) state comparison skipped - 'An arrival that does not match the challenge...'; (F12) nonce check skipped in exchange_code - 'An identity answering a stale challenge...'; (F13) signature not verified, or verification falls back to any key when the kid is unknown - 'An identity signed by an unknown key...'; (F14) issuer not validated - 'An identity vouched for by a different provider...'; (F15) exp not validated - 'An identity that has already expired...'.
steps.implementation_notes: PRODUCTION ALREADY SHIPPED: green-on-first-run is expected and must be recorded honestly; a failure must be a business failure; any production fix minimal. The mutation-relevant guard is that each scenario reaches the check it names: for F11-F15 the step must present a valid challenge cookie and the matching state (except the deliberately mismatched state of F11), otherwise every scenario is refused at 'no challenge cookie' and kills nothing beyond F10. A crafter may confirm this by checking the refusal reason in the 'oidc sign-in refused' log line, not by asserting on it. The double mints exp from the wall clock (now - 3600 for Lapsed) while the harness clock is MockClock at 2026-01-15; foundry-oidc validates exp against the wall clock, which is what makes the valid path green in the us-06 lane - if a lapsed identity is accepted, that is a genuine F15 defect, not a clock-fixture issue. No D3a interaction: all six refusals precede find-or-provision. OD-10 out of scope. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: Layer-3 example-based acceptance (Mandates 9/11). steps.scenario_name: Replaying a completed sign-in is refused
steps.description: Prove the three cross-cutting refusal properties of AC-3.5, AC-3.6 and AC-2.2/2.5/3.7. Named faults the 3 scenarios must kill: (F16) the callback ignores a failed code exchange, or a refusal flushes or rotates the caller's existing session - replay scenario; (F17) an unreachable provider surfaces as a 500, an unwrap panic, or a boot-time discovery dependency that stops other pages - unreachable scenario; (F18) any refusal branch differs from a wrong password in status or body (e.g. a 400/403 branch, a reason-specific message, the no-workspace branch rendering differently) - identical-refusal scenario.
steps.implementation_notes: PRODUCTION ALREADY SHIPPED: green-on-first-run is expected and must be recorded honestly; a failure must be a business failure; any production fix minimal. Replay (AC-3.5, feature-delta Changed Assumptions): the challenge cookie IS cleared on success, so the replay step must keep the original challenge cookie and state from the first round-trip and present them again with the same code - otherwise the refusal comes from 'no challenge cookie' and F16 survives. 'Their original session is untouched' replaces its placeholder panic! with: the session cookie from the first sign-in still opens the board after the replay. Unreachable: the provider is connected first (spawn_with_oidc builds lazily - no network at construction), then shut down; start then fails at discovery and refuses; the When must tolerate start returning a refusal without a Location. Identical refusals: compare bodies with the CSRF token masked (refuse() mints a fresh token when no CSRF cookie is carried) and compare against a real wrong-password POST /sign-in for an unknown address, as the provisioning module's turned_away Then does. The refusal page rendered by refuse() omits the cluster-identity control (render_signin_form passes offer_oidc=false) exactly as the wrong-password page does - this is what makes them identical; do not 'fix' it in this step. No D3a interaction: the collected variants all refuse before find-or-provision. OD-10 out of scope. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: Layer-3 example-based acceptance (Mandates 9/11). ENVIRONMENT: CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_BUILD_OVERRIDE_STRIP=false for cargo builds on this host; warm the acceptance binary first; acceptance uses a prebuilt foundry binary for subprocess lanes; bound every lane run with a timeout. GUARD LANES: keycloak-sso tag lane; keycloak-sso-provisioning (us-06) lane; cargo xtask check-arch; cargo xtask smoke.

steps.scenario_name: The password door still opens while cluster identity is available
steps.description: Prove D2 (strictly additive, break-glass door) end to end: replace the flag-only Whens ('sign in with their foundry password', 'first operator claims the instance', 'sign out and sign in again') with real HTTP. Named faults the 3 scenarios must kill: (F19) the password door is disabled or gated when a provider is configured - first scenario; (F20) bootstrap or readiness consults the identity provider, so a claim fails while it is unreachable - second scenario; (F21) a federated sign-in links to or creates a different account than the password door reaches for the same address - third scenario.
steps.implementation_notes: PRODUCTION ALREADY SHIPPED: green-on-first-run is expected and must be recorded honestly; a failure must be a business failure; any production fix minimal. Reuse the shipped drivers instead of re-implementing them: password_attempt (provisioning module, or the us_06_signin helper) for the password door, and the us_05_bootstrap / feature_bootstrap_enum_oracle claim helpers for the claim (mint a bootstrap token, POST /bootstrap). 'Foundry is connected to the cluster identity provider' must therefore NOT seed a workspace or account itself - seeding belongs to the account Givens - or the claim scenario has nothing to claim. RISK FOR THE SHARED THEN: 'they arrive at their board signed in as themselves' asserts 303 with Location exactly '/', but the shipped bootstrap claim answers 303 to '/dashboard' (bootstrap.rs ~line 186). Whether '/dashboard' counts as 'their board' is an open question, raised to the orchestrator; do not edit Gherkin and do not weaken the shared Then for the other three scenarios. Acceptable resolutions are a step-module change that asserts each door's documented landing plus a working session, or a ruling that the scenario fails for a business reason. 'Either door leads to the same person': strengthen the shared Then (or a scenario-local world flag) to compare the session's user with the federated one; a bare 303 to '/' cannot kill F21. No D3a interaction: the account exists before either door is used. OD-10 out of scope. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: Layer-3 example-based acceptance (Mandates 9/11). ENVIRONMENT: CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_BUILD_OVERRIDE_STRIP=false for cargo builds on this host; warm the acceptance binary first; acceptance uses a prebuilt foundry binary for subprocess lanes; bound every lane run with a timeout. GUARD LANES: keycloak-sso tag lane; keycloak-sso-provisioning (us-06) lane; cargo xtask check-arch; cargo xtask smoke. USER DECISION 2026-10-03 (scenario 19 landing): the shared Then 'they arrive at their board signed in as themselves' checks each door's DOCUMENTED landing — `/` for the password and cluster-identity doors, `/dashboard` for the bootstrap claim (bootstrap.rs, pinned by us_05_bootstrap) — then follows the redirect with the session cookie and confirms the session is that person. The step must know which door was used (record it in world state); it must NOT accept /dashboard for the password or SSO doors. No production change, no Gherkin change.

steps.name: foundry records which accounts provisioning created
criteria: Migration 0017_users_provisioned_at.sql adds users.provisioned_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL (no default, no index) and, in the same forward-only transaction, marks every password-less account with provisioned_at = created_at; accounts with a password, and an account reset before the upgrade, stay unmarked; a re-run changes nothing (DDD-23, DDD-24, OD-14)

An account is read as provisioned, by email and by id, when it carries the marker OR has no password (the rolling-deploy window row); an account with a password and no marker is read as not provisioned (DDD-26)

Provisioning a newcomer records the marker from the caller's injected clock in the same transaction as the user and the membership; the already-exists re-read writes nothing; no reset, password change or sign-in clears the marker (DDD-25, DDD-27, D9)
Readiness refuses against a schema that lacks users.provisioned_at instead of serving 500s at both sign-in doors (DDD-32), proven by a store test in the probe_schema_scoping.rs pattern

The three users_provisioned_at.rs scaffolds are un-ignored with their shims replaced by the real API and pass; no SCAFFOLD marker or DELIVER: note for DDD-25 remains in that file, provision_federated_member.rs or the scenario-18 Given
No acceptance scenario un-pended; keycloak-sso lane 37/37, keycloak-sso-provisioning lane 14/14 examples and us-06 lane stay green; fmt, clippy -D warnings, check-arch pass
steps.description: Store foundation for D3b, no behaviour change at either door yet. NOT a validation-only step: files_to_modify is non-empty — a new migration, the store read model and provisioning write, the probe, and the compiler-driven callers of the changed provision_federated_member signature. Write 0017 (ADD COLUMN plus the OD-14 backfill from created_at), add UserRow.provisioned computed in SQL as provisioned_at IS NOT NULL OR password_hash IS NULL in both find_user_by_email and find_user_by_id (the DDD-26 OR rule), add a `now` parameter to provision_federated_member and write provisioned_at in its existing INSERT on the Created path only, and add the users.provisioned_at assertion to Store::probe beside the 0006/0007 column checks. Fix every caller of the new signature: oidc::provision passes state.clock.now() (mechanical; the callback's decision logic is NOT touched here), the four calls in crates/foundry-store/tests/provision_federated_member.rs, the scaffold call in users_provisioned_at.rs and the scenario-18 Given 'the newcomer was given an account while provisioning was still switched on' in feature_keycloak_sso_provisioning.rs — each marked 'DELIVER:' where DISTILL left one. Un-ignore the three store scaffolds: the_upgrade_marks_exactly_the_password_less_accounts_as_provisioned_when_they_were_created (OQ-6), an_account_is_read_as_provisioned_when_marked_or_password_less (OQ-7), no_password_write_clears_the_provisioned_marker (DDD-25/27). Named faults this step's tests must kill: backfill marks password accounts, or uses now() instead of created_at (OQ-6 test); the DDD-26 'OR password_hash IS NULL' arm dropped so a window account reads as invited (OQ-7 test, by email AND by id); marker not written by the provisioning INSERT (DDD-25/27 test); marker cleared by reset_password_and_consume or update_user_password (DDD-25/27 test; scenario 14 kills it end to end in 04-02); probe silent on a pre-0017 schema (new DDD-32 probe test).
steps.implementation_notes: Latest migration is 0016_nullable_password_hash.sql; 0017 is forward-only with no down migration (a revert is a forward migration) and runs in one sqlx transaction under MIGRATION_LOCK_ID; no CONCURRENTLY. The backfill predicate is exactly `password_hash IS NULL AND provisioned_at IS NULL` and the value is created_at, never now() (DDD-24). OD-14 assumption is verified in DESIGN: every non-provisioning users INSERT binds a non-optional hash, so NULL hash means provisioned. The timestamp comes from the injected Clock (the reset_password_and_consume `now` convention), never SQL now() (DDD-25); FederatedProvisionOutcome is unchanged; the ON CONFLICT (email_lower) DO NOTHING re-read writes nothing (DDD-16). UserRow is built in only two places (store lib.rs ~1131 and ~2751); the compiler finds the rest. signin::submit_signin, submit_forgot and submit_reset ignore UserRow.provisioned (DDD-31) — do not branch on it at the password door. Nothing may write provisioned_at except the 0017 backfill and the DDD-25 INSERT (DDD-27); OQ-8 (an optional xtask check-arch scanner that rejects an UPDATE of provisioned_at under crates/) may be added here, it is not required — the store test is the floor. The DDD-32 probe test is not scaffolded by DISTILL; add it beside the existing cases in probe_schema_scoping.rs (or a sibling file with a WHY-NEW-FILE header if that file's harness does not fit). The scenario-18 Given passes harness(world).app.state.clock.now() (or the harness equivalent); its Gherkin is not touched. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: store integration tests over real Postgres are example-based (the OQ-6/OQ-7 rows are a declared mixed-row universe asserted in full, re-run idempotence included); the OR rule is a two-input boolean fully enumerated by the OQ-7 rows. ENVIRONMENT: build with CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_BUILD_OVERRIDE_STRIP=false on this host; warm the acceptance binary first (cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --test acceptance --no-run), and rebuild foundry before any lane that launches it (acceptance uses a prebuilt binary); bound EVERY lane run with timeout and kill leftover containers if it hangs; a testcontainers PortNotExposed failure is an infrastructure flake — rerun the affected crate's tests alone before treating it as a regression. GUARD LANES: cargo test -p foundry-store (all tests, incl. users_provisioned_at, provision_federated_member, nullable_password_hash, probe_schema_scoping); FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=keycloak-sso; FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=keycloak-sso-provisioning; FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=us-06 (password door, forgot, reset stay untouched); cargo xtask check-arch.

steps.name: Callback refuses a provisioned account whose provision role is withdrawn
criteria: Un-pends, one at a time in this order (6 scenarios, 7 examples): 'A provisioned member whose provision role is withdrawn is turned away and keeps everything they had' (primary); 'A provisioned member left holding only a different role is turned away' (2 examples); 'A member turned away after the withdrawal is let back in as the same account once the role is granted again'; 'A provisioned member who chose a password through a reset is still turned away without the role'; then the callback-arm guards 'An invited member without the provision role still signs in through the identity provider' and 'With provisioning switched off a provisioned member signs in whatever roles they hold'

A provisioned account whose ID token lacks the exact configured realm role is refused with no session, byte-identically (CSRF masked) to a wrong password; it keeps one account, one member membership in the original workspace, its name and its authored issue and comment (AC-7.1, AC-7.2, D7, D8)

Re-granting the role lets the same user id back in with no second account; a reset does not lift the refusal (AC-7.3, AC-7.5); an invited account without the role and any provisioned account with the provision role unset still link (AC-7.4, AC-7.9, D3b, OD-13)

The verdict is a pure judge_returning(provisioned, provision_role, identity) sibling of judge_newcomer, reading provider.provision_role() at sign-in time and matching via has_realm_role (DDD-29, D11, OD-9); the refusal rides the single refuse() with a new const 'provisioned account lacks provision role' distinct from LACKS_PROVISION_ROLE (DDD-30, AC-7.6)

The oidc.rs scaffold a_returning_account_is_refused_only_when_provisioned_and_the_role_is_missing is un-ignored, its shim and test-local literal deleted in favour of judge_returning and the new const, and passes all 10 rows plus the assert_ne!

steps.scenario_name: A provisioned member whose provision role is withdrawn is turned away and keeps everything they had
steps.description: Primary step for US-07: split DDD-15 step (1) in oidc::callback per DDD-28. On Ok(Some(u)) call judge_returning(u.provisioned, provider.provision_role(), &identity): (1a) not provisioned -> link, role ignored; (1b) provisioned, role unset -> link; (1c) provisioned, role held -> link; (1d) provisioned, role missing -> refuse(&state, &headers, PROVISIONED_LACKS_PROVISION_ROLE). Everything before step (1) keeps its order (challenge cookie, state, code, exchange + RS256 + nonce, email_verified); steps (2)-(5) are unchanged and the Existing outcome of step (5) is NOT re-judged. Scenarios 11-14 are RED today for MISSING_FUNCTIONALITY ('a refusal must not establish a session'); drive them GREEN one at a time. Scenarios 17 and 18 are GREEN_ALREADY guards for arms 1a and 1b; they are un-pended in THIS step (an adjustment to a 15-18-together split) because DISTILL's open item says un-pend the guards with 11 and these two pin exactly the arms this step's change can break. Named faults this step's tests must kill: role check skipped for provisioned accounts (11, 12a/b, 13, 14; unit rows 8-10); check applied to non-provisioned accounts (17; unit rows 1-3); role unset treated as refuse for provisioned accounts (18; unit rows 4-5); role match not exact — case-insensitive or client roles count (12b 'Foundry-User'; unit row 10); role held but still refused, or a second account created (13; unit rows 6-7); marker cleared by reset, end to end (14); refusal reason leaks or the response differs from a wrong password (11, 12, 14 byte-identical, CSRF masked); reason reuses LACKS_PROVISION_ROLE (unit assert_ne!); refusal deletes or alters account, membership, name, issues or comments (11's four Thens).
steps.implementation_notes: Callback is crates/foundry-app/src/oidc.rs (callback ~line 164, step (1) ~line 199, reason consts ~line 223, judge_newcomer ~line 273, scaffold test ~line 370-420). judge_newcomer cannot be reused: its None role answers NO_ACCOUNT, while a returning provisioned account with None must link (OD-13). Contract shape: judge_returning is pure, return-only, no I/O; the callback stays the imperative shell. Unit test: delete judge_returning_scaffold and PROVISIONED_LACKS_ROLE_REASON, call judge_returning and the production const; keep the 10-row table and the assert_ne! verbatim otherwise. AC-7.6's distinct reason is proven at unit level (the lane captures no tracing, D3a precedent); 'nothing added to the response' is the byte-identical comparison in 11, 12 and 14. Gherkin is DISTILL-owned: remove only ' @pending' from the 6 tag lines, text otherwise byte-identical. Scenario 13's Given composes 11's When and refusal, so it goes RED->GREEN with 11's fix; record honestly if it is green on the first run after 11. Scenarios 17 and 18 are expected GREEN on first run — record them as GREEN_ALREADY guards in the RED/GREEN log, never fabricate a RED. D11 renamed-role case has no scenario (harness cannot restart over the same schema); unit rows 8-10 cover it. No production change in signin.rs, reset_password.rs or admin_cli.rs (DDD-27, DDD-31). EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: Layer-3 acceptance over real HTTP and real Postgres is example-based (Mandates 9/11); the judge_returning unit test is a full enumerated table over its (provisioned, role, held) domain at the boundary values, following the shipped judge_newcomer idiom. ENVIRONMENT: CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_BUILD_OVERRIDE_STRIP=false for cargo builds on this host; warm the acceptance binary first (cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --test acceptance --no-run) — a cold binary makes subprocess scenarios time out; rebuild foundry before lanes that launch it; bound EVERY lane run with timeout (e.g. timeout 900) and kill leftover containers if it hangs; testcontainers PortNotExposed is an infra flake — rerun the crate alone. phases.name: Structural guard for the provisioned marker (OQ-8)

steps.name: check-arch forbids clearing or rewriting the provisioned marker
steps.description: OQ-8: enforce D9 (the provisioned marker is permanent; reset, password change or sign-in never clears it) structurally. Add an xtask check-arch rule, in the style of the DDD-22 no-board-keydown rule, that fails the build when any SQL UPDATE assigns users.provisioned_at outside the one sanctioned place: migration 0017's backfill. The only legitimate writer at run time is the INSERT in Store::provision_federated_member.
criteria: cargo xtask check-arch fails, naming file:line and D9, when any .rs file under crates/ or any .sql migration other than 0017_users_provisioned_at.sql contains an UPDATE that sets provisioned_at (case-insensitive, across line breaks within one SQL string or statement)

Migration 0017's backfill UPDATE and the INSERT that writes provisioned_at in provision_federated_member are not flagged; mentions in comments (// or -- or /* */) and in test files under crates/*/tests/ are not flagged
The rule scans by globbing crates/**/*.rs and crates/*/migrations/*.sql (no hand-maintained list) and fails closed if a directory cannot be read

Injected-violation gold tests in xtask cover: an UPDATE ... SET provisioned_at = NULL in a .rs string (flagged); a multi-line UPDATE users\n SET password_hash = $1, provisioned_at = NULL (flagged); the same text in a // comment (not flagged); a new migration 0018 that updates provisioned_at (flagged); 0017's backfill (not flagged); an INSERT naming provisioned_at (not flagged)
